html:
The great temple of Jupiter Best and Greatest on the Capitoline Hill in Rome, dedicated by tradition in 509 BCE, the first year of the Republic. It was the centre of Roman state religion.

The kings began it, especially the Tarquins, and it was built in the Etruscan manner: wide, on a high stone platform, with deep columns at the front and a roof of brightly painted terracotta. It housed three gods, Jupiter in the middle with Juno and Minerva on either side. A terracotta statue of Jupiter was said to be the work of Vulca of Veii, an artist from the Etruscan cities.

New consuls made vows there each year, and generals celebrating a triumph ended their parade at its steps. The temple burned down in 83 BCE, 69 CE and 80 CE, and each time it was rebuilt on the old plan, finally in marble. Its platform is still visible today. It was built in the same age as the Cloaca Maxima, soon after the fall of the kings.
sum: The great temple of Jupiter Best and Greatest on the Capitoline Hill in Rome, dedicated by tradition in 509 BCE, the first year of the Republic. It was the centre of Roman state religion.
